# Fig Performance

> Private one-on-one personal training gym in Placentia, California, for adults over 40 who want to lose fat, build muscle and get stronger. Coached by Daniel Figueroa ("Coach Dan"), an ACSM certified personal trainer and Precision Nutrition Level 1 certified nutrition coach. Progress is measured with InBody body-composition scans, and semi-private clients get red light and vibration therapy for recovery.

- Address: 1284 E. Yorba Linda Blvd, Placentia, CA 92870
- Phone: (714) 396-7178
- Email: trainat@figperformance.com
- Staffed hours: Monday to Friday 5 AM to 8:30 PM, Saturday 5 AM to 12 PM, closed Sunday. Personal training is by appointment.
- Serves: Placentia, Yorba Linda, Brea, Fullerton, Anaheim Hills and Villa Park (Orange County, CA)
- Reviews: 74 reviews of Coach Dan in total (checked Nov 24, 2026): 5.0 on Google with 23 reviews of Fig Performance, 5.0 on Yelp with 39 reviews (that page is now named FIG PERFORMANCE at 1284 E. Yorba Linda Blvd, Placentia; the reviews were earned under the business's former name, Train With Dan) and 12 more five-star reviews from people Dan coached before opening Fig Performance
- Price: two ways to train. One-on-one personal training is $60 to $90 a session, billed weekly or monthly, with a 3-month minimum; the exact rate depends on how often you train and whether you pay in full, and it is given in writing at the free consult. Semi-private small-group training starts at $180/month (1x a week), then $225 (2x), $279 (3x) or $345 (4x), with red light and vibration therapy included (3-month minimum, pause anytime). There is no membership or open gym option. No initiation fee. The first consult is free. Book it online: https://www.figperformance.com/#consult

## Guides for adults over 40

- [Fitness after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/fitness-after-40): index of all guides
- [Simple meal plan for weight loss + grocery list (free PDF)](https://www.figperformance.com/meal-plan-for-weight-loss): protein, carbs, fats and fiber at every meal; palm of protein, fist of vegetables, high-fiber carbs; breakfast, lunch, dinner and snack options; free PDF at https://www.figperformance.com/assets/fig-performance-meal-plan.pdf
- [How to lose 10 pounds in a month](https://www.figperformance.com/how-to-lose-10-pounds-in-a-month): realistic with about a 1,000-calorie daily deficit (500 food, 500 movement), high protein and strength training; about 8 lb fat plus water; client Adriana, 48, lost 10 lb in her first month
- [Dumbbell workout for beginners over 50](https://www.figperformance.com/dumbbell-workout-for-beginners-over-50): dumbbells and an adjustable bench, 2-3 days a week (full body every other day, full body 2x, or upper/lower); exercise menu by muscle; RPE 1-10 explained as reps left in the tank, aim 7-9; +2 reps or +5 lb a week when ready; shoulder, knee and back swaps; Sam, 70, started with dumbbells (15 reps, then 5, then 6-10) and now deadlifts 135 lb
- [Calorie deficit after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/calorie-deficit): weight loss is thermodynamics (Haub 2010 Twinkie diet: 27 lb in 10 weeks at 1,800 kcal/day, LDL -20%, HDL +20%); Coach Dan sets deficits from InBody BMR plus activity and job, usually 300-500 kcal/day, one-to-two-week test, weekly InBody; up to 1,000 kcal short-term only; plans built from foods clients already eat, more protein and fiber, 80/20; three new-year rules: get a coach, get a plan, do it
- [Hotel workout](https://www.figperformance.com/hotel-workout): Coach Dan trains on the road in any country by finding a gym nearby and buying a day or week pass (dumbbells, bench, cables; pull-up bar a bonus); 1-2 sessions a week keeps the routine; reps 12-25 with light dumbbells, 6-12 with heavier; room-only fallback circuit; pack gym clothes only; stock up on protein shakes, bars and snacks on arrival; protein floor on the road 100 g/day men, 80 g women (two shakes, a bar or Greek yogurt, dinner with protein and fiber); holiday travel: walk daily, pick drinking nights, book the first session back
- [Building muscle after 50](https://www.figperformance.com/building-muscle-after-50): realistic gains (Peterson 2011: ~2.4 lb lean mass in 20 weeks on average; ~1 lb/month early for people who never trained hard); recovery takes longer after 50 (2-3 lifting days, never back to back, 7+ h sleep); protein at goal weight in grams (PROT-AGE floor 1.2 g/kg if active); creatine monohydrate 5-10 g/day, safe for healthy adults (Antonio 2021, ISSN 2017), benefits for older adults and possibly memory
- [Strength training for women over 60](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-for-women-over-60): same formula as everyone, different starting point; heavy lifting for bone (LIFTMOR 2018: +2.9% spine BMD); balance = isometrics, eccentrics, unilateral leg work (Cochrane 2019: exercise cuts falls 23%, with strength ~34%); protein at goal weight in grams (PROT-AGE floor 1.0-1.2 g/kg), fiber 22 g+ for women 51+; Teresa 60: first pull-up in ~3 months, benches ~85 lb; Danielle: isometrics and unilateral work after a car accident left her tripping
- [Is belly fat the last to go?](https://www.figperformance.com/is-belly-fat-the-last-to-go): yes, the lower belly; the body stores reserves around the organs; visceral fat is lost first (Chaston 2008), lower-abdominal fat cells resist lipolysis (Wahrenberg 1989); cortisol and central fat (Epel 2000); InBody visceral fat target under 6; crunches don't burn fat (Vispute 2011) but weighted core work builds definition; walk 30 min daily, lift 2x/week, goal-weight protein; Priscilla, over 42, lost 20 lb and flattened her stomach in 2-3 months
- [Hip thrust form and why women over 40 need it](https://www.figperformance.com/hip-thrust): setup (bench 12-24 in, bar at hip crease with thick pad, knees at 90 degrees), full hip extension, power up, squeeze throughout; 3 leg days a week with hip thrust + squat + hinge + abduction, ~32 leg sets a week (Bret Contreras seminar, Aug 2026); client went 55 lb to 135 lb in six weeks
- [Are Jefferson curls safe?](https://www.figperformance.com/jefferson-curls): Coach Dan Jefferson curls 205 lb; loaded spinal flexion trains the range daily life uses; start at body weight to a bench, add range then 2.5 lb steps, 1-8 slow reps; cautions for osteoporosis and disc injury; Jonathan, 43, from back pain to 135 lb
- [Strength training for seniors](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-for-seniors): Coach Dan's approach for adults 65+: assess, then train push, pull, squat, hinge, carry and overhead; 8-10 reps then lower reps and heavier weight; add 2 reps or 2.5-5 lb a week; client results (Randy 73 benches 135 with shoulder arthritis)
- [How to lose belly fat after menopause](https://www.figperformance.com/how-to-lose-belly-fat-after-menopause): research-backed plan for women after menopause: strength training with progressive overload 2-3x a week, a small calorie deficit with whole fiber-rich foods, at least 1.2 g/kg protein, creatine 5 g a day, daily walking, sleep, and asking a doctor about hormone therapy
- [GLP-1s and muscle loss](https://www.figperformance.com/glp-1-muscle-loss): how to keep muscle on semaglutide or tirzepatide: protein at least goal weight in grams, lifting 2-3x a week, enough calories, daily walking, and habits for after stopping
- [Strength training for women over 50](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-for-women-over-50): age doesn't decide the program, the assessment does; menopause, bone density (LIFTMOR), protein; clients Teresa (60) and Sam (70)
- [Workout plan for men over 40](https://www.figperformance.com/workout-plan-for-men-over-40): train for function, start light, fix neck, shoulders, back, hips and knees; client Jonathan, 43, went from back pain to a 185 lb bench
- [Tib raises](https://www.figperformance.com/tib-raises): why the tibialis anterior matters for shock absorption, knees and shin splints; wall tib raises, kettlebell toe raises, tib bar; 5-30 reps
- [3-day workout split for beginners](https://www.figperformance.com/3-day-beginner-workout-plan): why full body 3 days a week works, and links to the women's and men's plans
- [Beginner workout plan for women](https://www.figperformance.com/beginner-workout-plan-for-women): Coach Dan's 3-day full-body plan: 4 leg and glute exercises (squat or lunge, hinge, hip thrust, abduction last), 2 upper body, 1 core (2 sets) a day, rest 1:15-2 min, warm-up, exercise guide with easier and at-home versions
- [Beginner workout plan for men](https://www.figperformance.com/beginner-workout-plan-for-men): Coach Dan's 3-day split: 2 leg exercises and 1 calf exercise first each day, chest/back/shoulders on days 1 and 3, arm day in the middle, wall tib raises, 2 core sets, rest 1:15-2 min
- [How to avoid holiday weight gain after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/how-to-avoid-holiday-weight-gain): Coach Dan's rules: protein first, room for dessert (he eats 80/20), train on Thanksgiving, set drink boundaries, keep each holiday to a few days, plus a hotel workout
- [How to lose weight after 40](https://www.figperformance.com/how-to-lose-weight-after-40): Coach Dan's plan for busy professionals: daily steps, protein, lifting heavy enough, training twice a week, hormones, and body recomposition
- [Can you build muscle after 60?](https://www.figperformance.com/build-muscle-after-60): yes, with two client examples (Teresa, 60, first pull-up in about 3 months; Sam, 70, deadlifting 135 lb for reps) and the exact progression used
- [Why am I not losing weight?](https://www.figperformance.com/why-am-i-not-losing-weight): Coach Dan says you're almost always not in a true calorie deficit; nine reasons (portions, protein at 0.7-1 g per lb, progressive overload, daily steps, sleep, stress, measuring, medical) and what to do about each
- [Strength training for women over 40](https://www.figperformance.com/strength-training-for-women-over-40): how often to lift, what to do, how heavy, and a sample week

## Client case studies

- [Client case studies](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies): index of all nine, fat loss, strength and training around pain, studio and online
- [Jonathan, 43](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/jonathan): ex-Army, a new son, a stiff and achy back and a sore shoulder; had quit golf. Pull-ups 1 to 5, chin-ups with +35 lb, Jefferson curl 135 lb, bench 185 lb, and back on the golf course. Studio
- [Rosa, 43](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/rosa): 205 to 169 lb in 11 months. Long shifts, home hungry with dinner undecided; had tried cutting carbs, shakes and a boot camp. Two studio times she could usually make plus a few dinners she could grab on the way home. Studio
- [Ray, 64](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/ray): 218 to 183 lb in 10 months. Walked mornings, did yard work, had not lifted in years and had started asking for help carrying things. Lifting twice a week, morning walks kept. Studio
- [Chris, 50](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/chris): 224 to 193 lb in 9 months. Trained well at home, lost the routine on work trips. A home lifting plan plus a short dumbbell workout for hotel days and a few reliable restaurant orders. Online
- [Matt, 39](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/matt): 212 to 184 lb in 7 months. Lifted in his twenties, then work and kids; a 30-day challenge and strict meal prep both failed when his schedule moved. Two sessions he could usually make and a shorter workout for busy weeks. Studio
- [Jenna, 34](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/jenna): 172 to 154 lb in 6 months. Had a gym membership but used the treadmill and the same machines; uncomfortable learning a new lift in a busy weight room. Learned to set up lifts, choose a starting weight and progress. Studio
- [Linda, 57](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/linda): 149 to 143 lb in 6 months. Walked with friends and rarely missed a class, but had used the same dumbbells for years. Kept what she enjoyed and added tracked lifts. Studio
- [Eric, 52](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/eric): 181 to 176 lb in 8 months. Ran and lifted when he could; added sets, swapped exercises from videos and tried a six-day split, but work trips broke the rhythm. A shorter plan with the same key lifts logged weekly. Online
- [Natalie, 38](https://www.figperformance.com/case-studies/natalie): 137 to 134 lb in 7 months. Pilates, weekend runs and occasional lifting; wanted definition, and more cardio with smaller portions left her flat. Regular lifting, tracked. Three pounds on the scale, a visible change in shoulders and legs. Online
